description_full: Tanger Inc. is a leading owner and operator of outlet and other open-air retail shopping destinations, with 45 years of expertise in the retail and outlet shopping industries. Tanger's portfolio of 38 outlet centers and four open-air lifestyle centers includes nearly 17 million square feet well positioned across tourist destinations and vibrant markets in 22 U.S. states and Canada. A publicly traded REIT since 1993, Tanger continues to innovate the retail experience for its shoppers with over 3,000 stores operated by more than 800 different brand name companies. Tanger is furnishing a Form 8-K with the SEC that includes a supplemental information package for the quarter ended June 30, 2026. Tanger Inc. was established in 1981 and was incorporated in North Carolina.

culture_narrative: Employs approximately 407 people. Revenue per employee of $1.4M ranks in the below the sector median among Real Estate peers. Each employee generates $726K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $31K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 2× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags low compensation governance risk (1/10).
financial_summary: Tanger Inc. is a mid-cap real estate business with a $4.6B market cap on $582M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +10% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 6% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests. Gross margins of 69% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $295M in free cash flow — roughly 51 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.57× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 5.1× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 2.7× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield is only 1.4%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 2.4% of the shares, and within its sector the business captures 1.5× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
